answer: Each identity registers one leg-ringed falcon nesting on a glacier cliff and locks 70 bonds at a jetty registry. It records the ring number, glacier cliff survey, and nesting season; a jetty warden checks the ring against the survey and falcon breeding log, and a duplicate ring or mismatched cliff burns the bond. The first pair costs 36, the kth 36+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6030 and 1000 fake pairs cost 3,033,000 in fees. A rented falcon fails because one falcon cannot nest on two cliffs in one season, so a second registration burns. An honest keeper pays 36 once and redeems the bond.
